_meta: A small grayscale image and some rectangular regions to sum. image is a grid of pixel intensities. A box blur (or any box filter) replaces each pixel with the average over a square window around it, which means summing every pixel in that window -- naively k*k additions per output pixel for a k-wide window, so cost grows with the window area. A summed-area table (integral image) precomputes, once, the sum of every top-left rectangle, so afterwards the sum over ANY rectangle is four array lookups via inclusion-exclusion, independent of the rectangle's size. windows lists (row0, col0, row1, col1) half-open rectangles to sum both ways and confirm they agree. blur_sizes lists window widths k for the cost comparison. Every sum and operation count here is computed exactly.
